title: Delegated PD backend architecture research and implementation gate
body:
## Goal

Determine where PD currently creates unique value in the backend architecture, where additional PD use can materially improve it, and where PD would instead add duplication, recursion, cost, or architectural bloat.

This issue is the delegated research and recommendation owner. Issue #70 remains the implementation and backend-maintenance owner.

## Gate 0 — justify this process before operationalizing it

The first bounded research job is not to change the backend. It is to determine whether this delegated PD-backend process itself merits persistent operation.

Compare at least these alternatives:

1. no new delegated process;
2. event-triggered PD-backend review;
3. lower-frequency periodic review;
4. hourly review.

Do not activate a recurring process merely because useful PD opportunities exist.

A persistent process is admitted only when independently frozen evidence establishes:
- unique material gain over the current architecture/workflow;
- a smaller or cheaper intervention does not capture the same gain;
- recurring cost and recursion burden are bounded;
- protected behavior is non-regressive;
- interaction with existing ImprovementCore, AuditCore, TransferCore, task-entry/tool-selection, capture, and issue #70 is non-duplicative;
- an independent challenge survives;
- relevant OPEN coordinates do not undermine the decision.

Otherwise disposition is RESEARCH_ONLY, KEEP_CURRENT, REJECT, or OPEN.

## Operating architecture

Use IC-017 semantic preflight and IC-011 adaptive capability selection.

Do not automatically run the whole toolkit on every candidate.

For each live problem/opportunity:

FREEZE TARGET/BASELINE/PROTECTED BASIS
→ TYPE LOAD-BEARING PRIMITIVES
→ IDENTIFY LIVE BOTTLENECK
→ SELECT ONLY CAPABILITIES THAT CAN MATERIALLY CHANGE IT
→ GENERATE CANDIDATES/RIVALS
→ TEST UNIQUE GAIN, COST, PRESERVATION, AND ABLATION
→ INDEPENDENT CHALLENGE
→ RECOMPUTE/RESELECT WHEN STATE CHANGES
→ TERMINAL VERIFICATION
→ DISPOSITION

IC-017, IC-011, PD/AuditCore, ImprovementCore, HF-001, multi-object/relational PD, Raise-the-Ceiling, TransferCore, A16, and other toolkit capabilities remain selectable. Their use is result-sensitive rather than mandatory.

## Research scope

Map current backend PD use and classify each location as:
- demonstrated useful use;
- duplicated/overlapping use;
- obsolete use;
- missing high-value use;
- cost exceeds demonstrated value;
- attribution unresolved.

Search for upstream interventions whose correction removes multiple downstream failures.

Use current PD research as it develops, including semantic typing, result sensitivity, hidden selectors, recursive PD, relational/multi-object PD, dependency/spine work, ablation, and capability-selection research.

Preserve OPEN and incomparability.

## Recommendation gate

A recommendation may be handed to issue #70 only when it demonstrates:
- exact problem/opportunity;
- baseline and protected behavior;
- selected intervention and why it is the smallest sufficient intervention;
- unique incremental gain;
- explicit costs;
- alternatives and ablation evidence;
- regression/invalidation conditions;
- independent challenge result;
- verification requirements.

Allowed dispositions:
- RESEARCH_ONLY
- KEEP_CURRENT
- REJECT
- OPEN
- HANDOFF_TO_ISSUE_70

HANDOFF_TO_ISSUE_70 requires the implementation gate to pass strongly.

## Coordination with #70

This issue has no routine implementation authority.

Issue #70 owns backend mutation, implementation, integration, CI/repository repair, and implementation verification.

When a recommendation passes the gate, this issue sends #70 a bounded implementation packet. #70 can reject, modify, reopen, or return the packet when implementation evidence changes.

## Anti-bloat rule

The existence of an applicable PD capability is not evidence that it belongs in the backend.

Prefer the smallest intervention that demonstrates unique result-sensitive gain.

Research without implementation is a successful outcome.

## Initial bounded task

1. Build the evidence-backed map of current backend PD use.
2. Identify plausible missing high-leverage uses.
3. Audit those recommendations.
4. Independently audit the audit/recommendation chain.
5. Evaluate whether this delegated process itself merits persistence.
6. Compare no-process, event-triggered, lower-frequency, and hourly variants.
7. Do not activate recurrence until this Gate 0 evaluation produces a strongly supported implementation recommendation.
8. If Gate 0 passes, hand the implementation packet to #70 and only then establish the justified cadence.

## Provenance

This architecture incorporates the result of running the proposal through IC-017 and IC-011: semantic preflight precedes operation, capability selection is adaptive and bottleneck-relative, full-toolkit invocation is not automatic, independent challenge is required, and the recurring process itself is treated as a candidate intervention rather than a presupposition.
